Akira

Katsuhiro Otomo’s 1988 animated film of his manga, set in a Neo-Tokyo of densely drawn night towers, through which motorcycles leave trails of colored light.

Source
Wikipedia: Akira (1988 film)
Creator
Katsuhiro Otomo (director); Tokyo Movie Shinsha (animation studio)
Made
1988 (released 16 July 1988); the manga began in 1982
Style
Cyberpunk (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods

Evidence
Based on the Wikipedia articles on the film and on cyberpunk, read as wikitext on 2026-10-02. No image of the film was inspected for this record.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia: “The Japanese cyberpunk subgenre began in 1982 with the debut of Katsuhiro Otomo’s manga series Akira, with its 1988 anime film adaptation (also directed by Otomo) popularizing the subgenre.” Cyberpunk.

The film was animated by Tokyo Movie Shinsha and distributed by Toho. Wikipedia: “The British Film Institute describes Akira as a vital cornerstone of the cyberpunk genre, along with Blade Runner and Neuromancer.” Wikipedia).

Dave Kehr of the Chicago Tribune praised its “animation-specific ideas: Vehicles leave little color trails as they roar through the night”. Wikipedia).

Why it belongs

Akira adds speed and violence to the night city of Blade Runner. Its light trails are an early form of the style’s motion: light that smears as it moves.

It ties the style to Japan and to animation, which later games and anime continued.

Borrow

Show motion as a trail of colored light behind a moving element, not as a blur of the whole scene.

Draw a city as a mass of many small lit windows to suggest scale and density.
